 Blakely rises to the top in Rotterdam World women’s all-around final
 IG Staff
 Saturday, October 24, 2026
 Skye Blakely (USA) 
 American Skye Blakely delivered a composed and consistent performance across all four apparatus to capture the women’s all-around gold medal at the 2026 World Championships in Rotterdam on Friday, scoring 55.733 to claim the biggest individual title of her career.
 Russia’s Liudmila Roshchina , competing under the WG2 designation, earned silver with 55.199, while China’s Ke Qinqin took bronze with 55.032. Algeria’s Kaylia Nemour , the top qualifier and one of the leading favorites for gold, finished a heartbreaking fourth with 54.998, just 0.034 behind Ke.
 Blakely established herself as the gymnast to beat from the opening rotation, producing an excellent double-twisting Yurchenko vault for 14.200. She followed with a well executed uneven bars routine, showing precise handstands, clean releases and a stuck dismount to earn 14.400 and take the lead after two rotations with 28.600.
 The two time U.S. World team gold medalist (2022, 2023) strengthened her position on balance beam, delivering one of the finest routines of the evening for14.200, extending her advantage to more than a point heading into the final rotation.
 Needing only a solid floor exercise to secure the title, Blakely delivered under pressure, scoring 12.933 to complete a four-for-four performance and claim the gold medal.
 Roshchina remained within striking distance throughout the competition, opening with a 14.033 on vault and following with a strong 14.333 on uneven bars. She continued with one of her best balance beam performances of the championships, scoring 13.433, before finishing with a strong floor routine for 13.400 to secure the silver medal, her first ever medal from a World championship.
 Ke also remained in contention throughout the final, highlighted by a 14.033 on vault and 13.900 on uneven bars. Despite a fall on her double back dismount on balance beam, she earned 13.833, keeping her medal hopes alive. A clean floor routine, scoring 13.266, ultimately secured the bronze medal by a narrow margin ahead of Nemour.
 For Nemour, the competition took an unexpected turn on the opening event. The Paris Olympics uneven bars gold medalist, who entered the final with the highest combined difficulty among the leading contenders, mistimed her approach to the vaulting and was forced to compete a layout instead of the planned double-twisting Yurchenko. The resulting 12.366, with a difficulty value of just 3.6 compared with her intended 5.0, immediately left her chasing the leaders.
 Nemour fought back on uneven bars, earning 14.866 despite an early missed connection that forced her to add an extra kip cast to handstand. She then produced an outstanding balance beam routine for 14.500, the highest score on the apparatus of the all-around competition, moving back into medal contention. However, her final total of 54.998 left her agonizingly close to the podium, which is a repeat result from one year ago.
 Japan’s Aiko Sugihara finished fifth with 54.765 following a consistent competition highlighted by a 14.266 on vault. France’s Elena Colas placed sixth with 54.666, delivering four solid routines, including a 14.433 on uneven bars and 13.933 on balance beam.
 American Claire Pease finished seventh with 54.232. She opened with a strong uneven bars routine for 13.833 but lost ground falling on her beam series. Pease recovered with 13.733 on floor exercise and 14.133 on her Cheng vault for 7 th place at her first ever World championships. Spain’s Alba Petisco rounded out the top eight with 54.198.
 The World Championships continue tomorrow with the first day of individual event finals (floor, pommel horse and rings for the men and vault and uneven bars for the women).
